object_description: stacked pavilion-like lower masses with two upper building bodies
design_condition: Lower collective volumes are freely arranged in a pavilion logic while upper bodies align with the surrounding institutional complex and accommodate outdoor squares at different elevations.

positive.statement: The built masses are established with great mastery through rigorous placement and contextualized dimensioning.

position.rationale: Two upper bodies and stacked lower masses are clearly legible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The project forms a link and continuity between two previously separate built fabrics.

position.target: link and continuity between built fabrics
position.rationale: The central overlap between offset mass groups provides the most plausible connecting zone.

positive.statement: The programmatic layout across different ground levels is remarkable.

position.rationale: Lower and upper mass groupings visibly establish a stepped arrangement across the sampled model.

positive.statement: The project develops a critical, current, and responsible view of territorial construction.

position.rationale: The broad site-level judgment is anchored to the distributed pavilion footprint and lower landscape-like masses.

negative.statement: The identical typology produces an excessively banal arrangement of endless corridors.

position.rationale: Interior circulation is not distinguishable, so it is approximated within the larger upper-body zone.

negative.statement: The interior spaces do not provide the qualities expected of a place of study and exchange.

position.target: interior spaces for study and exchange
position.rationale: Interior qualities are absent from the exterior sample; the marker estimates a central upper-body interior.

negative.statement: The program is resolved functionally but with insufficient sanitary, technical, and vertical-circulation provision.

position.rationale: Unmodeled service systems are approximated near the eastern building body.

negative.statement: Natural lighting on the floors is insufficient.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal levels are visible in elevation and associated with the offset plan masses.

negative.statement: The double-skin facade is incomprehensible in principle and prohibitive for the expected energy performance.

position.rationale: The south-facing envelope is visible, but a distinct double-skin layer cannot be identified.

negative.statement: The large excess floor area and substantial structural demands raise fears of a high construction cost.

position.rationale: Cost and structural burden apply globally; no useful spatial referent is stated.
